name: Report crypto disposals on IRS Form 8949 (short vs long term)
goal: Classify crypto disposals (sell for USD, crypto-to-crypto, spending crypto), split short-term vs long-term holding periods, select the correct 1099-B checkbox when no broker form exists, and fill description/dates/proceeds/basis/gain rows (optionally via tax-software CSV).

source.title: How To Report Crypto On Form 8949 For Taxes | CoinLedger

constraints: Educational self-custody/tax procedure only — not financial advice; no coin tips or return promises.
Ground every step in YouTube-provided captions; portable UI names OK when vendor chrome drifts.
Never digitize a seed phrase or enter it into a website/phone camera.
Not tax advice — form mechanics only.
USD buys are not disposal rows; sells/trades/spending are.

steps.action: List disposals only: sell→USD, trade crypto→crypto, or spend crypto. USD purchases are not 8949 disposal rows.
Bucket by holding period: <12 months short-term section; >12 months long-term section.
If no crypto 1099-B (historically common), select the checkbox for transactions not reported on 1099-B (often C or F per instructions). If a broker 1099-B applies, choose the matching box instead.
Fill each row: description, date acquired, date sold, proceeds, cost basis, gain/loss. Example: buy BTC $300 → trade for ETH worth $400 (BTC disposal) → sell ETH $600 (ETH disposal).
Optional: reconcile via crypto tax software and export Form 8949 / tax-software import instead of hand-typing.

verification: Crypto→crypto trades produce a disposal of the given asset
